meta.title: Ship Details — hulls, enchanted devices, laboratories
meta.source: Foundry VTT REST API (arm5e system), pulled 2026-07-13
meta.fleetNote: Regardless of type or quality, each ship in the flotilla has a capacity of around 125 tonnes and a crew of 13 including the captain. None of the ships have so far been enchanted or opened for enchantment by a Hermetic shipwright; each can be affected by the standard Hermetic Structure Target. Ships run approximately 75 ft long, 25 ft in the beam, and just over 12 ft keel to deck, with a cargo hold and single deck — the magus’ laboratory typically occupies the rear of the cargo hold.

tide-of-memory.dimensions: 75 ft long, 25 ft in the beam, 12 ft keel to deck.
tide-of-memory.description: A mysterious cog of lost paths and unanswered questions. Sometimes, it is seen docked in multiple ports at once, and those who board alone claim to hear conversations from the past drifting through the timbers. With Solving’s disappearance, the ship feels adrift in more ways than one, and none dare to say how long it will remain in this world.

enchantedDevices.name: Bell of Summoning
enchantedDevices.description:
Commissioned from a Verditius working out of Verdi, when rung this bell sounds throughout all six ships of the fleet, using up six of its 12 uses. This allows the bell to be rung twice with effect.

The bell is usually rung twice in succession, once to alert the magi and again to give them chance to locate the direction of the magic using their Magical Astrolabes, described below

enchantedDevices.name: The Magical Astrolabe
enchantedDevices.description:
When used against an active magical effect, the astrolabe allows the user to determine the horizontal and vertical directions of the magic’s origins. It cannot provide distance information.

The device is used to locate the source of the sound of the Bell of Summoning. When used in conjunction with charts, this provides a confident view on where the bell is.

Each ship in the fleet is issued with one of these devices.

enchantedDevices.name: The Master's Chart
enchantedDevices.description:
Solving possesses an arcane connection to each ship in the fleet in the form of a carved miniature made from the wood of their frames. When these are individually placed onto this enchanted map, which is the triggering mechanism, the miniatures sail to their appropriate locations.

Dustin has a copy of the laboratory text for this device, which was commissioned from a magus of Verdi in the Roman Tribunal.

The chart has two effects. The first finds the fleet through individual arcane connections to the vessels placed upon the chart. The second uses the information provided by the first to move these wooden tokens to their appropriate place on the chart.

The large chart of wood and parchment has been opened with eight pawns of vis and the two enchantments currently use four of those pawns.

effects.name: Finding the Fleet
effects.description: Provides information on the location of a target ship given an arcane connection to it.

effects.name: Mark the Fleet
effects.description: Moves the token placed upon the chart to the location indicated by the Finding the Fleet effect

brineborn.dimensions: 75 ft long, 25 ft in the beam, 12 ft keel to deck.
brineborn.description: An English hulk that seems more water than wood, its hull damp even in full sun. It never fully resists the ocean, instead moving with the waves like a living thing. Some claim it was once a drowned vessel, raised by magic, and that it still remembers the seabed. When anchored, the ship sways as though still at sea, unsettling those unaccustomed to its nature.

enchantedDevices.name: The Ever-Full Grain Dish
enchantedDevices.description:
Willhelm Stienauer's personal magic item — carried with him, not fixed to any ship (recorded here because he sailed aboard the Brineborn on the 1224 Ireland voyage). A carved stone dish about the size of a large butter dish that is perpetually full of grain: pour it out and it refills as fast as it is emptied (a sack or two a minute by hand), never emptying in any practical span.

Mechanism (his graduation thesis): a DELAY-CAST spell that delays not in time but in VOLUME. The grain-creation itself is a Creo Herbam Ritual (a non-standard, "virtual" effect), wrapped in a standard Hermetic delay-cast on a whole-Ring duration that re-fills the dish over and over until the spell's stored volume is exhausted — so it is "ever-full" only up to a very large but finite reserve, not literally infinite. The stored volume is given inconsistently in play — ~a million cubic yards (05-23 session) vs. ~six million (06-20 session) — so treat it as "several million cubic yards, minus the little poured out so far."

Because the grain is magically created, it counts as magically-produced content in every Tribunal (see the Rule of Silver, Reference → Homebrew), so it cannot be freely sold as mundane trade goods without inviting a jurisdictional-arbitrage question. Willhelm treats it as unremarkable and tends to mention it only in passing.

scholars-wake.dimensions: 75 ft long, 25 ft in the beam, 12 ft keel to deck.
scholars-wake.description: A Flemish cog with a broad deck and reinforced cabins, designed for research and magical experiments at sea. It carries an extensive collection of arcane instruments, and its hold is filled with alembics, scrolls, and preserved specimens. The crew has standing orders never to open certain doors, as some sections of the ship’s hold contain unstable magical phenomena.

the-gloaming.dimensions: 75 ft long, 25 ft in the beam, 12 ft keel to deck.
the-gloaming.description: A Breton ketch that thrives in twilight, its sails shimmering with strange, near-invisible patterns that shift in the half-light. When night falls, the ship sometimes drifts beyond the reach of reality, its position uncertain until dawn. Faeries recognize it not as a threat, but as an enigma—it never arrives unannounced, yet no one ever sees it coming.

maelstroms-maw.dimensions: 75 ft long, 25 ft in the beam, 12 ft keel to deck.
maelstroms-maw.description: A Nordic buss that seems defiant even in calm waters, always leaning slightly into the wind as though eager to challenge the storm. Its figurehead—a snarling beast of uncertain origin—has eyes that glow faintly when tempests rise. The ship’s crew swears that, in the worst of gales, they hear a voice calling commands that none of them spoke.
